notes.title: Anti-Cheat, Mods, Linux, and Steam Deck
notes.notes:
[p][b]Hello, racers![/b][/p][p]We see your questions and concerns about the addition of Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) to the game. We understand that changes can be worrying, especially for mod enthusiasts and Linux/Steam Deck players. Let’s go over the key points together.[/p][p][b]Why did we need EAC?[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Cheating prevention[/b] [/p][p]We are working on new competitive modes. Unfortunately, cheaters (e.g., those using "infinite nitro") ruin the experience for fair players and prevent you from fully enjoying new features.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Your feedback[/b][/p][p]We constantly receive reports about cheaters—both in ranked races and regular lobbies.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Why EAC?[/b] [/p][p]We chose EAC as one of the least intrusive options among popular anti-cheat solutions. EAC does not block ReShade and does not interfere with car appearance mods.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Why did mods stop working?[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Data system update[/b][/p][p]Issues with car appearance mods are not caused by EAC but by our internal data storage system update. We made this change so that after version 1.7.0, modders would need to update their mods less frequently with our releases.[/p][/*][*][p][b]ReShade[/b][/p][p]Currently, ReShade works, but crashes may occur. Keep in mind that ReShade is a third-party tool, and we cannot guarantee its stability. However, our team is already investigating these crashes to improve compatibility where possible.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Why were there issues with Linux and Steam Deck?[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Linux[/b][/p][p]Initially, CarX Street was not positioned as a game with Linux or third-party emulator support. However, given your interest, we have already started adapting the game for Linux systems.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Steam Deck[/b][/p][p]Partial Deck support, which existed before version 1.7.0, was restored in patch 1.7.1. We are aware of complaints about unstable performance and are actively working on optimizing the game for Steam Deck. Note that full official Deck support was never previously announced, but we are striving to achieve it.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Will EAC be removed from the game?[/b]
No, EAC will remain. It is necessary to protect fair play and the future development of multiplayer. We believe this is an important step toward creating a fair and enjoyable environment for all players.[/p][p][b]Thank you for your understanding and patience![/b] We will continue listening to your feedback and working to improve CarX Street.[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: About Anti-Cheat and Mods
notes.notes: [h2][b]About Anti-Cheat and Mods[/b][/h2][p][/p][p][b]Steam Deck & Linux[/b][/p][p]The team is preparing a fix for this temporary issue in the coming days.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Anti-Cheat[/b][/p][p]Anti-cheat is not designed to block players or their accounts—it exists to prevent game hacking. Of course, if you try to run the game with Cheat Engine enabled, you won’t be able to play, but your account won’t be banned. You simply won’t be able to launch the game until you close Cheat Engine. Don’t fear anti-cheat—it’s not your enemy. It protects you in multiplayer and poses no threat to honest players.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Mods[/b][/p][p]As we’ve already announced, visual mods such as texture replacements, car model swaps (FBX), and ReShade presets are not penalized in our game. Regarding broken mods—we’ve improved mod support in update 1.7.0 by changing the car mesh storage system. This means mod creators won’t have to update their mods after version 1.7.0.[/p][p][/p][p][b]ReShade[/b][/p][p]Unfortunately, ReShade support is currently suspended, but the team is actively looking into bringing it back. For now, we recommend removing ReShade, as it may cause serious graphical artifacts or game crashes.[/p]

notes.title: Update 1.6.0
notes.notes:
[b]What’s up, drivers! 1.6.0 Update of CarX Street PC is available.[/b]

In the new version

[b]New Features:[/b]

Inventory added: your inventory allows you to store, install, and sell the parts you acquire as you play the game. Your engines and transmissions will also be moved to your inventory when you swap cars.

Multiplayer user rooms added: you can now create a public room in multiplayer mode. You can also create rules for the room - mono- or multi-class, front- or rear-wheel drive, day or night - it's all up to you.

Prototype parts added: take your tuning to the next level! These parts will allow you to get every last drop of performance out of your cars. Prototype-class parts can be found in Elite Club Races.

[b]Improvements:[/b]

Phone calls added before and after races with the Club Bosses of Wild Juniors, Union Underground, Burnout Rangers, Kanjo Spirit, and Street Hunters.

Boss and underboss cars now have new looks! Each car has its own style that highlights its club's unique personality.

Club postgame progress enhanced: leveling up in the postgame now earns you new car parts.
Reward for Club Bosses and Underbosses enhanced. Now when you win against them, you can get parts for your cars. If you already completed the clubs, don't worry - when you enter the game, you'll automatically get all Street Packs for clubs in your inventory.

New cars earned for completing clubs: the cars you earn are now more interesting and compelling. If you've already completed the clubs that unlock the new cars, don't worry - they'll be added to your account automatically next time you log in.

StreetNET League cars improved.

New StreetNET League races added for the mountain region and Sunset Speedway racetrack. New cars have also been added in the new races.

Enhanced mod support: community-created mods will no longer be deleted or broken when the game is updated.

Performance improved.
In-game cameras improved.
Racing wheel force feedback improved; new settings added.
Club Race difficulty adjusted.
Advanced smoke effect improved.
Car behavior improved.
Cost of tuning cars reduced.
Clutch-type differentials upgraded.
Option to turn off counter steering on sticks added.
Support for trigger vibrations on Xbox One and Xbox Series X controllers added.
TAA Upscaling resolution scaling system added.
TAA anti-aliasing improved; ghosting effect from cars removed.

[b]Fixes:[/b]

The difficulty level descriptions in the settings menu no longer cause the game to hang.
Smoke under the wheels of boss cars in cutscenes now displays properly.
Boss cutscene audio fixed.
Radial menu mouse behavior fixed.
Loading screen logo fixed.
SI5 and DX7 prototype engines from Drift Cars add-on fixed.
Dynostand settings save window fixed.
TCL ECU icons fixed.
White tire trails fixed.
Collision sound effects fixed.

notes.title: 1.2.1 Update announcement
notes.notes:
[b]What's up, drivers! On Friday, the Street PC 1.2.1 update was released, and many of you had questions about why the Sunset Speedway DLC wasn’t included in the Deluxe Edition on Steam. Here’s our response:[/b]

You’re absolutely right — on the release date, August 29, 2024, it was planned for the Sunset Speedway DLC to be part of the Deluxe Edition, with the total price of the bundle set at $29,99.

Unfortunately, during the DLC’s launch on Steam, a technical error occurred — the platform did not include Sunset Speedway in the Deluxe Edition and automatically reduced the price of the bundle from $29,99 to $21,68 without notifying us. As a result, the information during the first two hours after release was inaccurate.

Attempts to resolve the issue were unsuccessful, so the Sunset Speedway DLC was removed from the Deluxe Edition description, as it could no longer be included.

We understand that those who purchased the Deluxe Edition within the first two hours of its release, expecting the Sunset Speedway DLC to be included, may feel disappointed. To address this, we are taking matters into our own hands. If you purchased the Deluxe Edition on August 29 between 10:00 AM and 12:00 PM (UTC+3), please contact our support team support@carx-tech.com with proof of purchase. We will provide you with a key for the Sunset Speedway DLC.

Please note that distributing the keys may take some time, as the process will be handled manually.

As compensation for the technical error and the incorrect description at the game’s release, 250 gold coins have been added to your Steam accounts.

[b]Let’s go over this again: Steam independently removed the Sunset Speedway DLC from the Deluxe Edition and immediately adjusted the price to $21,68. In other words, at the time of the bundle’s release, the Deluxe Edition no longer included the Sunset Speedway DLC, and the price reflected the contents of the bundle. Within two hours of the release on August 29, 2024, we updated the information in the description. From that point onward, the description on Steam no longer included the Sunset Speedway DLC, as you can see it now.[/b]

We apologize for the technical issue at launch and thank you for staying with us. We will continue to develop the game and add exciting new content!

notes.title: PC version FAQ
notes.notes:
What's up drivers!

Thanks a lot for all your feedback on CarX Street for PC release date announcement and to follow it up, we'd like to answer some of your most popular questions. 

[b]Will there be cross-progression between mobile and PC versions?[/b]

We don't have such plans, but we are looking into our options for providing mobile players with special rewards for purchasing PC version.

[b]How is PC version different from the mobile one?[/b]

First, we've completely reworked in-game balance for the PC version of the game: rewards were increased, so players could gain in-game currency the most comfortable way and there are no microtransactions in PC version.

notes.title: This week on the streets
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35655900/23fcf8b1c507502d46507afe20c6e69f2f5da332.png[/img]
Hey guys. As you know, last week we held the first of two scheduled news streams. It was very interesting to hear your opinion, and most importantly, to see your reaction to the presented information.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35655900/65b86dd8260ff4352ccd1de6061f61700c350534.png[/img]
We would like to thank the Russian-speaking part of our community for their activity and your questions.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/6JIzEwlFBv0Hz1G2fg/giphy.gif[/img]

Speaking of questions, we are ready to answer some of the most frequently asked:

[b]Question[/b]
What physics is used in the project?
[b]Answer [/b]
Based on CarX 

[b]Question[/b]
Will there be damage to parts in the tuning system?
[b]Answer [/b]
Yes, the damage sistem is planned.

[b]Question[/b]
How to get into closed beta testing?
[b]Answer [/b]
Follow the news. We will definitely tell you about the registration process for the closed beta version of the game.

[b]Question[/b]
Will there be police in the game?
[b]Answer [/b]
At the moment, we cannot give an answer to this question. But we want to assure you that we also want to implement police chases.

[b]Question[/b]
Will it be possible to call another player to the race?
[b]Answer [/b]
Yes, both in the open world and through special events.

[b]Question[/b]
Drift or racing
[b]Answer [/b]
Depending on car tuning and preferred driving style.

[b]Drive carefully, CarX Team[/b]

notes.title: Why release date is change
notes.notes:
[b]Why release date is change ?[/b]

Dear players. We seriously underestimated the amount of work at the start of the project, so we are forced to change the release date from November 5, 2020 to November 24, 2021. As always, we try to do the best for our fans, and we are obliged to reach a whole new level of quality of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35655900/145129824eddfae5f9657f756057412d5c1f78b2.png[/img]

The current work plan allows us to say with confidence that the selected date is more correct.

During the next year, we will actively inform you about our project development process.

Sincerely, CarX Street team.
